definitions.explanation: A general term for alcoholic beverages. The お is an honorific prefix.
Specifically refers to nihonshu, the traditional Japanese rice-based alcoholic drink.

examples.japanese: お{酒|さけ}は{飲|の}みますか。
お{酒|さけ}は{二十歳|はたち}からです。
examples.english: You can drink alcohol from age 20.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}のお{酒|さけ}を{飲|の}んでみてください。
お{酒|さけ}を{飲|の}みすぎて、{頭|あたま}が{痛|いた}いです。
examples.english: I drank too much alcohol and have a headache.

examples.japanese: {冷|つめ}たいお{酒|さけ}と{温|あたた}かいお{酒|さけ}、どちらがいいですか。
examples.english: Would you like cold sake or warm sake?

examples.japanese: お{酒|さけ}に{弱|よわ}いので、{少|すこ}ししか{飲|の}めません。
examples.english: I can't hold my liquor, so I can only drink a little.

examples.japanese: お{酒|さけ}を{控|ひか}えています。
このお{酒|さけ}は{辛口|からくち}です。
{地元|じもと}のお{酒|さけ}を{味|あじ}わいたい。
examples.english: I want to try the local sake.

examples.japanese: お{酒|さけ}を{飲|の}んだら{運転|うんてん}しないでください。
examples.english: Don't drive if you drink alcohol.

notes:
お{酒|さけ} has two meanings: (1) alcohol in general, and (2) specifically Japanese sake ({日本酒|にほんしゅ}). The お is an honorific prefix.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- お{酒|さけ}を{飲|の}む: to drink alcohol
- お{酒|さけ}に{強|つよ}い/{弱|よわ}い: to hold liquor well/poorly
- お{酒|さけ}を{控|ひか}える: to cut back on alcohol

TYPES OF SAKE:
- {辛口|からくち}: dry sake
- {甘口|あまくち}: sweet sake
- {冷酒|れいしゅ}: cold sake
- {熱燗|あつかん}: hot sake

LEGAL NOTE:
The legal drinking age in Japan is 20 ({二十歳|はたち}). {飲酒|いんしゅ}{運転|うんてん} (drunk driving) is strictly prohibited.
